headline: CRUDE RUNS 5% ON HORMUZ, SOY OIL BREAKS HARD
lead: WTI's at $92.61 overnight, up 4.9% after another tanker took fire off Qatar, the first deep-Gulf hit since fighting flared there back in September. Soybean oil got hit the other way, down 3.1% as meal took over the complex's weight. That split already moved crush margins before a single export sales number hit the tape.
teaser: Crude gains on fresh Hormuz tanker attacks while soybean oil breaks and meal takes the crush spread the other way.

one_number.context: Tanker traffic through the Strait dropped to its lowest in two months even as flows had been back near pre-war levels days earlier.

sections.title: Crude Runs On Fresh Tanker Hit
sections.body: - WTI's at **$92.61** overnight, up 4.9%, after a tanker took multiple projectile hits 51 nautical miles off Qatar, the first deep-Gulf strike in weeks.
sections.so_what: Diesel costs just got a fresh risk premium heading into fall fieldwork.

sections.title: Soy Oil Breaks, Meal Takes Over
sections.body:
- Soybean oil's down 3.1% overnight to **$67.42** while meal ran 3.5% higher to $365.90, the crush spread flipping hard toward protein.
- Soybeans themselves are soft, down 0.3% to $12.94, caught between the two product moves with no clean net direction.
sections.so_what: Crush margin math just moved without soybeans themselves doing much.

sections.title: Corn Grinds At The Round Number
sections.body:
- Corn's barely moved, up a half-cent to **$5.03**, holding the same ground it's traded since reclaiming $5 three sessions back.
- Grain storage is the live story underneath the calm: farmdoc's new read says Corn Belt capacity covers this year's carry-in plus harvest in aggregate, but ten of thirteen states show local shortfalls.
sections.so_what: Tight local storage is pressuring basis more than the futures chart admits.

outside_the_pit.title: Beef Exports Climb On Taiwan Demand, Pork Slips
outside_the_pit.body: August data shows beef exports rose on what exporters call outstanding Taiwan demand, while pork shipments to Mexico fell sharply versus last year.

watch_list.desc: Weekly export sales print; soybean sales under 1.5 MMT would read soft against the meal/oil split.
Hormuz tanker count; another attack pushes WTI toward $95, a calm week fades the premium back toward $88.
Gulf storm track; a hurricane landfall near shut-in platforms adds to crude's bid, a miss unwinds it fast.

daily_quote.text: Quality means doing it right when no one is looking.
